candidate_windows.window_text: For all tests, we train on 10 billion tokens using an Adam optimizer (Kingma and Ba, 2014) with a learning rate of 1e-4 that warms-up over the first $1\%$ of tokens and linearly decays after, batch size $= 128$ , max sequence length $= 128$ , $\beta_{1} = 0.9$ , $\beta_{2} = 0.999$ , L2 weight decay of 0.01, and a dropout probability of 0.1. In accordance with other papers, we use a gelu activation (Hendrycks and Gimpel, 2016). Using four p100 GPUs, it takes between 13 and 15 hours to train a model for each one billion token epoch depending on the tasks used.
